items.title: How Does the Book Empower Developers Beyond Apple Intelligence?
items.summary:
Apple Intelligence is useful, but developers need more than built-in features.

In this short, Keiji Kamigusa explains how Build Applications with Local AI Models on a Mac helps you go beyond using Apple’s AI tools and start building your own.

Instead of waiting for whatever features come packaged into the OS, you’ll learn how to run local models, create private chatbots, build RAG apps, work with documents, and experiment with AI workflows directly on your Mac.

That’s the real shift: from being an AI user to becoming an AI builder.

If you’re a developer on a Mac and want more control, privacy, and flexibility than any single platform can give you, local AI is where to start.

Learn more: https://hubs.la/Q04mY6wQ0

items.title: 2.8 Trillion Parameters - Kimi K3 is here
items.summary:
Kimi K3 is Kimi’s most capable model to date, with 2.8 trillion parameters. Built on Kimi Delta Attention, a hybrid linear attention mechanism, and Attention Residuals, it offers native visual understanding and a 1M-token context window for frontier intelligence scenarios such as software engineering, knowledge work, and deep reasoning.
In our evaluations, Kimi K3 delivers frontier-level performance. Among the models tested, its overall intelligence ranks second only to Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol. For the complete benchmark results, see our tech blog. The full model weights of Kimi K3 will be released in the coming days. More details on the architecture, training, and evaluation will be published together with the Kimi K3 technical report.


https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/kimi-k3-quickstart#introducing-kimi-k3

items.title: AI Agents Code Their Own Harness Optimization
items.summary:
What happens when a frontier LLM (GPT, Claude) is surrounded by an editable harness: and separate solver, debugger, and meta-agent roles are allowed to iteratively rewrite its prompts, memory, middleware, verification gates, tool interfaces, and control logic using execution traces and benchmark feedback? 

My video dissects the full outer-loop optimization system, formalizes how harness search differs from trajectory-level test-time scaling, and examines the experimental protocol required to determine whether recursive agent self-modification constitutes genuine architectural improvement ... or merely a more elaborate form of inference-time adaptation.

all rights w/ authors:
"Rethinking the Evaluation of Harness Evolution for Agents"
Yike Wang 1,2 Huaisheng Zhu1 3 Zhengyu Hu2 Yige Yuan2 Zhengyu Chen3
Shakti Senthil2 Hannaneh Hajishirzi2 Yulia Tsvetkov2 Pradeep Dasigi1 Teng Xiao1

items.title: How One Immigrant Used AI to Finally Be Understood
items.summary: In episode 1009 of the SuperDataScience Podcast, Jon Krohn talks with Steve Mock, Investor at Blumberg Capital about Kathy Jew's inspiring story from aisavedme.org, where she used AI to communicate complex ideas about her career change to her Chinese relatives who didn't speak English. This allowed her to feel 'fully understood by my family members' for the first time in years, demonstrating AI's profound ability to foster deeper human connections.

items.title: AMA with Luis Serrano 📱
items.summary:
Luis Serrano is an AI scientist and educator. Previously, he was a Machine Learning Engineer at Google and Lead Artificial Intelligence Educator at Apple.

In this session, we’ll ask these questions:
- Why does ML feel so intimidating to beginners?
- Who is Grokking Algorithms book really for?
- What is new in the latest edition of the book?
- Why do ML fundamentals still matter in the age of LLMs?
- Where should someone start with machine learning today?
- How can learners move beyond just copying tutorials?
- Why is visual intuition so important in ML?
- How do you explain overfitting in simple terms?
- How should beginners choose the right ML algorithm?
- Why is accuracy sometimes a bad metric?
- How much math do people really need for ML?
- How does the book make ML practical with Python?
- Why do neural networks feel like magic?
- What’s the simplest way to understand neural networks?
- What should readers be able to do after finishing the book?

This is a live, interactive session, bring your questions for Luis.

items.title: Early Access: Architecting for Autonomy 📱
items.summary:
Architecting for Autonomy teaches you how to update, adapt, and rebuild existing systems so that autonomous AI agents can operate safely and responsibly at scale.

In this session, we’ll ask Anjali & Philip these questions:
1. Why are enterprises struggling to move from AI pilots to real autonomous systems?
2. What’s the difference between automation, copilots, and true autonomy?
3. Where do traditional enterprise architecture models fall short with agentic AI?
4. What is the biggest mistake teams make when introducing autonomous agents?
5. How should architects decide what an AI agent should and shouldn’t be allowed to do?
6. How can enterprises avoid creating uncontrolled “shadow agents”?
7. What does good governance look like when agents can make decisions?
8. How do you design human oversight without slowing everything down?
9. What new security risks appear when agents act on behalf of users or systems?
10. How should companies manage agent identity, permissions, and trust?
11. What does Zero Trust mean in an agentic AI architecture?
12. How can teams make autonomous systems observable and auditable?
13. When does an autonomous system need a kill switch?
14. How should enterprises test agentic systems before putting them into production?
15. What skills do architects need now to design safe, scalable AI autonomy?

This is a live, interactive session, bring your questions for Philip & Anjali.
 
We will also giveaway Ebooks to 2 lucky winners during the session. Comment #AI to enter the raffle!

items.title: Mathematical Computation for the Age of Quantum and AI
items.summary:
This webinar is dedicated to the latest mathematical computation available in Wolfram Language 15. You will learn about a new suite of special functions motivated by Feynman integral computations in quantum field theory, a dedicated neural network for solving nonlinear differential equations and new special non-commutative algebras, along with deep advances related to plasticity, swirling flows and alternate coordinate systems in PDE modeling.
